# Tesla Magnetic Generator

> A DIY resource for building magnetic generators and going off-grid, based on Nikola Tesla's designs. Written by Jake Mercer, a DIY enthusiast and off-grid homeowner in rural Colorado.

## About

Jake Mercer is a DIY enthusiast who has built four magnetic generators and gone fully off-grid. This site covers the practical experience of building and running magnetic generators, comparisons with solar power, and honest answers to common questions about "free energy" devices.

## The Product

The build plans recommended throughout this site are packaged as the Complete Ultimate OFF-GRID Generator — a step-by-step DIY blueprint based on Nikola Tesla's suppressed magnetic generator designs. A companion video, presented by Michael Morgan, explains how Tesla's designs were suppressed and walks through what the plans cover.

## The 1894 File

- [Tesla's Earthquake Machine: What the 1893 Record Says](https://teslamagneticgenerator.com/tesla-earthquake-machine.html): The machine is real and the 1893 report is specific. The earthquake is a story Tesla told an interviewer in 1935, fifty years later.
- [Tesla's 1893 World's Fair Exhibit, Walked Through](https://teslamagneticgenerator.com/tesla-worlds-fair-1893.html): Most accounts of the 1893 Fair retell a publicity war. There is also a contemporary walkthrough of Tesla's exhibit, item by item, written by the man w
- [30,000 Alternations a Second: Tesla's Lost Generator](https://teslamagneticgenerator.com/tesla-high-frequency-alternator.html): Chapter XXIX of the 1894 volume describes rotary machines with hundreds of poles, built to make current at frequencies we would still call high. It al
- [The Paper Tesla Scribbled in Pencil: How AC Won](https://teslamagneticgenerator.com/rotating-magnetic-field-1888.html): The document that made alternating current usable was almost never read aloud. The man who edited the 1894 book had to persuade Tesla to give a paper 
- [Tesla Lit Lamps by Holding Them: The 1891 Proof](https://teslamagneticgenerator.com/tesla-lit-lamps-without-wires.html): Tesla lit lamps by holding them, in New York in 1891 and in London in 1892, and the 1894 book prints both lectures. It also prints the tests behind it: high potential, the insulated body as the return path, and a point where the light goes out.
- [Tesla's One-Wire Power: The Experiment Textbooks Skip](https://teslamagneticgenerator.com/tesla-one-wire-power.html): Tesla told the Institution of Electrical Engineers in 1892 that currents of high frequency and high potential let him work with one wire only, and the 1894 book prints the apparatus: a motor, an electrolytic cell and a lamp each worked from a single connection. It also prints his reason, an engineering one about the cost of copper, and the limits he put on it.
